proof:
Source: Step 6 of the parent proof (countable (m+1)-rectifiability of the product), with the null-set transfer (D1) taken as the hypothesis (NT).

Notation. E := ℝ^P = Eucl P, E′ := ℝ^{P+1} = Eucl (P+1), Hᵏ := μHE[k], equiv_n := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin n) ℝ : Eucl n ≃L[ℝ] (Fin n → ℝ); π(y) := equiv_P⁻¹(Fin.tail (equiv_{P+1} y)) = (y_1, …, y_P) for y ∈ E′. Further Φ(s, x) := equiv_{P+1}⁻¹(Fin.cons s (equiv_P x)) = (s, x_1, …, x_P) for s ∈ ℝ, x ∈ E, and y₀ := equiv_{P+1}(y)(0). (F1) Φ(y₀, π(y)) = equiv_{P+1}⁻¹(Fin.cons (equiv_{P+1}(y)(0)) (Fin.tail (equiv_{P+1} y))) = equiv_{P+1}⁻¹(equiv_{P+1} y) = y (ContinuousLinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, Fin.cons_self_tail, symm_apply_apply). (NT) is the hypothesis: for every N ⊆ E with Hᵐ(N) = 0, H^{m+1}({y ∈ E′ : π(y) ∈ N}) = 0 (the null-set transfer (D1) of the parent proof).

1. (Unpacking.) By CountablyRectifiable m M there are M₀ ⊆ E with Hᵐ(M₀) = 0 and maps F_j : Eucl m → E (j ∈ ℕ), F_j K_j-Lipschitz for some K_j ∈ ℝ≥0, with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j.
2. (Three linear maps.) Let hd : Eucl (m+1) → ℝ, hd(u) := u₀ = equiv_{m+1}(u)(0) (the coordinate projection 0 composed with equiv_{m+1}); tl : Eucl (m+1) → Eucl m, tl(u) := equiv_m⁻¹(i ↦ equiv_{m+1}(u)(i.succ)) = (u_1, …, u_m) (ContinuousLinearMap.pi of the projections i.succ, composed with equiv_{m+1} and equiv_m⁻¹); Ψ : ℝ × E → E′, Ψ(a, x) := Φ(a, x). Ψ is additive and homogeneous (apply equiv_{P+1}, which is injective, and compare coordinates with Fin.cases: coordinate 0 is a, coordinate k.succ is x_k), and ℝ × E is finite dimensional, so Ψ is a continuous linear map (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap). Every continuous linear map L is ‖L‖₊-Lipschitz (ContinuousLinearMap.lipschitzWith). (Explicitly |u₀| ≤ ‖u‖, ‖tl u‖ ≤ ‖u‖ and ‖Ψ(a, x)‖ = (a² + ‖x‖²)^{1/2} ≤ √2·max(|a|, ‖x‖), but only Lipschitz continuity is used.)
3. (The Lipschitz parametrizations.) Define G_j(u) := Ψ(hd(u), F_j(tl(u))) = Φ(u₀, F_j(u_1, …, u_m)). The map u ↦ F_j(tl(u)) is K_j‖tl‖₊-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.comp); the pairing u ↦ (hd(u), F_j(tl(u))) ∈ ℝ × E is max(‖hd‖₊, K_j‖tl‖₊)-Lipschitz for the product (max) distance (LipschitzWith.prodMk); hence G_j is ‖Ψ‖₊·max(‖hd‖₊, K_j‖tl‖₊)-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.comp). In particular ∃ K, LipschitzWith K G_j for every j.
4. (The exceptional set.) Put C₀ := {y ∈ E′ : π(y) ∈ M₀} (a full cylinder, not intersected with any slab). By (NT), H^{m+1}(C₀) = 0.
5. (Covering.) Let y ∈ E′ with π(y) ∈ M. If π(y) ∈ M₀ then y ∈ C₀. Otherwise π(y) ∈ range F_j for some j, say F_j(w) = π(y) with w ∈ Eucl m. Put u := equiv_{m+1}⁻¹(Fin.cons y₀ (equiv_m w)) ∈ Eucl (m+1). Then hd(u) = y₀ (apply_symm_apply, Fin.cons_zero) and tl(u) = w (equiv_m is injective; coordinatewise Fin.cons_succ), so G_j(u) = Φ(y₀, F_j(w)) = Φ(y₀, π(y)) = equiv_{P+1}⁻¹(Fin.cons (equiv_{P+1}(y)(0)) (Fin.tail (equiv_{P+1} y))) = y (F1: apply_symm_apply, Fin.cons_self_tail, symm_apply_apply). Hence y ∈ range G_j.
6. (Conclusion.) {y : π(y) ∈ M} ⊆ C₀ ∪ ⋃_j range G_j with H^{m+1}(C₀) = 0 (Step 4) and every G_j : Eucl (m+1) → E′ Lipschitz (Step 3); this is the definition of CountablyRectifiable (m+1) {y : π(y) ∈ M}. ∎

  obtain ⟨M₀, hM₀, F, hF, hcover⟩ := hM

key_steps: Unpack M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃ range F_j with Hᵐ(M₀) = 0 and F_j Lipschitz.
G_j(u) := Φ(u₀, F_j(u_1,…,u_m)) is a composition of continuous linear maps (hd, tl, Ψ) with F_j, hence Lipschitz (prodMk, comp).
If π(y) = F_j(w) then G_j(equiv⁻¹(Fin.cons y₀ (equiv w))) = Φ(y₀, π y) = y, so the cylinder is covered.
